Finished 21:02 EST (deadline 21:30). No earlier statement of Theorem B or Theorem A was found in any source I read. theoremBKnown = no-evidence-found. This is not conclusive: several sources stayed out of reach (see notChecked).

What the sources say about additivity or unions of universally null (UN) sets, all read from fetched text:

1. Fremlin, Measure Theory, vol. 5, chapter 54 (draft dated 23.10.14/17.9.16), 544K and 544L. The earlier agent's report is confirmed. 544L(a) states: for a metrizable space X, with Un the sigma-ideal of universally negligible subsets, add(Un) >= add(N_omega). This is a lower bound only. Fremlin gives no upper bound for add(Un), no link to d or cof(N), and no statement that uses the existence of a large universally negligible set. So add(N) <= add(UN) (Goto, Corollary 5.13) is already in Fremlin, for all metrizable spaces.

2. Fremlin, chapter 43, section 439. 439C(b) says the universally negligible subsets form a sigma-ideal. 439C(c) is a general form of the note's Lemma 3: if Y is universally negligible, f : X -> Y is Borel measurable and every fibre is universally negligible, then X is universally negligible. 439G uses 439C(c) to show that the graph of a bijection onto a universally negligible set is universally negligible; this is the argument behind Goto's Claim 5.5.1 (F2 in the note). The note's Lemma 3 and (F2) are therefore classical.

3. Miller's Handbook chapter (read through OCR of the scan on his site), Section 7 "Unions": the universal measure zero sets are closed under countable unions, and under Martin's Axiom under unions of fewer than continuum many. No upper bound. Lemma 9.3.1 there (a one-to-one continuous preimage of a universal measure zero set has universal measure zero) is another classical form of Lemma 3.

4. Miller's 1993 survey "Special sets of reals" (TeX source): nothing on unions or additivity of universal measure zero sets.

5. Reclaw, Colloq. Math. 62 (1991): "additive" there means algebraic sums X+Y, not unions. Its Theorems 1 and 2 assume a UN set of size c and diagonalise against all Borel sets, using an injective-preimage lemma. This is the closest precedent in method to Theorem B, but the result is different and add(UN) does not appear.

6. Reclaw, Real Anal. Exchange 27 (2001/02): if a sigma-ideal J with Borel basis containing singletons has add(J) = kappa, there is a UN set of size kappa. Nothing on add(UN).

Searches for the phrases "union of universally null sets", "additivity of universally null", "additivity of the ideal of universally", and "universally null sets" with "cof(N)" in OpenAlex full text gave 0 results. StackExchange API (MathOverflow and Math.SE) gave 0 results. arXiv: Goto's paper is still at v4 (9 Oct 2026); no later arXiv abstract with "universally null" concerns add(UN). Web search returned only Goto's paper and Fremlin's chapter 54.

Consistency check: nothing read contradicts Theorem A or B. The MA statement in Miller agrees with Theorem B, since MA gives add(N) = c.

Suggested edits to the note's literature section: (i) replace "reported, not checked" for Fremlin 544L(a) by "checked"; (ii) cite Fremlin 439C(c)/439G and Miller's Lemma 9.3.1 as the classical source of Lemma 3 and (F2); (iii) mention Reclaw 1991 as a related diagonalisation over a UN set of size c.

Downloaded files are in scratch/dl (Fremlin chapNN.pdf/.txt; subfolders miller, reclaw, papers). No file in the open-logic-24 folder was edited.

findings.source: D. H. Fremlin, Measure Theory vol. 5, Chapter 54 (PDF draft headed 'Version of 23.10.14/17.9.16'), 544K, 544L and the section notes
findings.statement: 544K: if X is metrizable and mu is a sigma-finite Borel measure on X, then add N(mu) >= add N_omega. 544L(a): if X is metrizable and Un is the sigma-ideal of universally negligible subsets of X, then add Un >= add N_omega. 544L(b): the union of fewer than add N_omega universally measurable subsets of X is universally measurable. Proof of (a): apply 544K to each Borel probability measure that is zero on singletons. The notes to section 544 say 544K-544L depend on the Gitik-Shelah theorem via 544Ha (if an atomlessly-measurable cardinal exists, add N_omega <= non N_omega = omega_1). No upper bound on add Un is stated anywhere in the chapter; 'universally negligible' occurs only in 544L. I did not look up Fremlin's definition of N_omega; chapter 55 (552O proof) says the Lebesgue null ideal is isomorphic to N(nu_omega).

findings.source: Fremlin, Measure Theory vol. 4, Chapter 43, section 439 (439B, 439C, 439F, 439G, 439X, 439Y, notes)
findings.statement: 439B defines a Hausdorff space as universally negligible if it carries no Borel probability measure that is zero on every singleton. 439C(b): the universally negligible subsets of a Hausdorff space form a sigma-ideal. 439C(c): if Y is universally negligible, f : X -> Y is Borel measurable and each fibre is universally negligible, then X is universally negligible (general form of the note's Lemma 3). 439F(c): Grzegorek's theorem, a universally negligible subset of [0,1] of size non(N). 439G: the graph of a bijection from a non-null set of size non(N) onto a universally negligible set is universally negligible, by 439C(c) (the argument of Goto's Claim 5.5.1). 439Xg: the product of two universally negligible spaces is universally negligible. Section 439 has no statement about unions of uncountably many universally negligible sets and no cardinal additivity.

findings.source: Fremlin, Measure Theory, Chapters 41-49 and 51-56 (text extracted with gs, searched for 'universally negligible', also with words run together)
findings.statement: Other occurrences, none about additivity: 534H (strong measure zero sets are universally negligible) and exercises 534Xa, 534X(e),(g); 552O(a) (under a measure-extension hypothesis, a universally negligible second-countable space has size < cov N(mu)); 553D (after adding kappa > c random reals, every universally negligible subset of {0,1}^omega has size < c); 553O (2^{non N} <= number of universally negligible sets <= 2^c, before the Larson-Neeman-Shelah theorem); one use of 439Cb for a union of two sets in Chapter 45; one exercise in Chapter 47. Chapters 51, 52 and 56 contain no statement on universally negligible sets. Exercise in Chapter 53 (line near 531-532 exercises): the union of fewer than add N universally Radon-measurable sets is universally Radon-measurable, under a Maharam-type hypothesis; this is about measurability, not negligibility.

findings.source: A. W. Miller, 'Special subsets of the real line', Handbook of Set-Theoretic Topology (1984), 201-233; scan from Miller's site, read through tesseract OCR
findings.statement: Section 7 'Unions' says the families of universal measure zero sets, perfectly meager sets and several others are closed under countable unions, and that under Martin's Axiom 'countable' can be replaced by 'fewer than continuum' for universal measure zero and perfectly meager sets. Theorem 5.4 is Grzegorek's theorem. Lemma 9.3.1: a one-to-one continuous preimage of a universal measure zero set has universal measure zero. Section 5 says that in the random real model every universal measure zero set has size at most omega_1 (attributed to Baumgartner and Laver). No upper bound on the additivity, nothing resembling Theorem A or B. Caveat: read from OCR, so a missed sentence is possible; I searched the OCR for 'union' and 'additiv' and read every hit.

findings.source: A. W. Miller, 'Special sets of reals', in Set Theory of the Reals (Israel Math. Conf. Proc. 6, 1993), 415-432; TeX source survey.tex
findings.statement: The only passage on universal measure zero sets is the section 'Universal measurable sets': Mauldin's question on the number of universally measurable sets, Laver's result that consistently there are only continuum many universal measure zero sets, and the Grzegorek-Ryll-Nardzewski theorem. Nothing on unions or additivity.

findings.source: I. Reclaw, 'Some additive properties of special sets of reals', Colloq. Math. 62 (1991), 221-226 (PDF from the Reclaw publications page)
findings.statement: 'Additive' means algebraic sums. Lemma 1(b): under an independence hypothesis, Y = {x + d_x} is a one-to-one Borel preimage of X, so Y is universally null if X is. Theorem 1: if a universally null set of size c exists, there are a Borel measure mu and a universally null Y such that every Borel B covering Y has mu(B+t) = 1 for some t. Theorem 2: for suitable universally null X of size c there is a universally null Y with X+Y not universally null. Theorem 3: under MA, for every X of size c there is a universally null Y with X+Y not universally null. Theorem 5: two universally null Q-linear subspaces with non-universally-null sum. The proofs index all Borel sets by a universally null set of size c and use the injective-preimage lemma, as Theorem B does with cof(N). No statement on unions of many universally null sets or on add(UN).

findings.source: I. Reclaw, 'On a construction of universally null sets', Real Anal. Exchange 27 (2001/02), 321-323
findings.statement: Theorem 1: a set well ordered by a universally measurable relation is universally null. Theorem 2: codes of a family of Sigma^0_alpha sets well ordered by inclusion form a universally null and universally meager set. Corollary 1: if a sigma-ideal J with Borel basis containing singletons has add(J) = kappa, there is a universally null and universally meager set of size kappa. Final remark: in models with no universally null set of size c, no such ideal has additivity c. Nothing on the additivity of the universally null ideal itself.

findings.statement: Abstract only: each analytic set in R^n contains a universally null set of the same Hausdorff dimension; similar results for metric spaces and universally meager sets. The abstract does not mention unions or additivity. Full text not read. Zindulka's arXiv:1208.5521 was downloaded and searched: no statement on universally null sets.

verify.notes:
Finished 21:00 EST (deadline 21:35). I found no error in Lemmas 1-3, the proof of Theorem B, or Corollaries (a)-(c) of notes/partial-results.md. Every step was re-derived by hand; the Lemma 2 constants and the second-moment identity were also checked by exact computation. No file in the folder was edited.

(i) Hidden measurability. None found.
- Lemma 2: every set that is measured (K, T^n(s), E(s), R, W, A, Q_n) is closed or clopen. K is never claimed independent of anything; it enters only through Cauchy-Schwarz against 1_K.
- Lemma 3: X and P are arbitrary sets and are only covered by Borel sets. nu(B) = mu(Delta ∩ phi^{-1}[B]) is defined for Borel B only.
- Theorem B: X_f and the union {w_beta} are arbitrary sets. The argument uses only "a set meeting every K_beta is not contained in any G_beta" and outer measure.
- Lemma 1: the G_xi may be arbitrary null sets; only open supersets are measured.

(ii) Definition match. It matches.
- flat.txt, Introduction: a subset of 2^omega or omega^omega is universally null if it has outer measure zero for every atomless finite Borel measure on that space. Section 2: Meas(2^omega) is the set of atomless finite Borel measures on 2^omega. Section 5 notes the zero measure is allowed and harmless.
- Lemma 3 quantifies over exactly these measures on 2^omega. Its removal of the countable atom set is the same device as Goto's own Claim 5.5.1.
- Two points are implicit in Lemma 3 but correct. A finite Borel measure on 2^omega with no point masses is atomless (an atom concentrates on a decreasing sequence of cylinders, hence on a point). nu_0 may be the zero measure, and then B = 2^omega works.
- add(I) in Goto's Definition 5.1 is the least size of a subfamily with union outside I, as the note uses it.

(iii) Consistency with Goto and standard models. No contradiction found. Standard-model values are from memory, not fetched.
- Goto proves add(N) <= add(UN) = add(UN,N) <= add(SN,N) (Prop. 5.12, Cor. 5.13, Section 5.6). flat.txt contains no model where add(UN) or add(SN,N) differs from add(N); that is Question 6.3.
- Goto Cor. 5.19 model: Goto gets add(UN) = aleph_1 with non(N) = c = lambda. Then cof(N) = non(N), so Corollary (a) gives add(UN) = add(N) = aleph_1. Agrees.
- Cohen and Hechler models (aleph_2 reals over GCH): add(N) = aleph_1, non(N) = cof(N) = c = aleph_2, so Theorem B gives add(UN) = aleph_1. Independently, Goto Thm 5.17/5.18 (theta_0 = theta = aleph_1, lambda = aleph_2, sigma-centered iterands) gives add(UN) <= add(SN,N) <= aleph_1. Agrees.
- Random, Laver, Miller, Sacks and Goto's PT_{f,g} model: non(N) = aleph_1, so add(N) = add(UN) = aleph_1 by ZFC bounds alone.
- Miller model: Theorem B's hypothesis holds by Goto Thm 2.6 (a UN set of size aleph_2 = c = cof(N)) although non(N) < cof(N), and the conclusion holds by the previous line. This is an independent check in a model outside Corollary (a).
- MA: add(N) = c, so both sides are c.
- Mathias model: add(N) = aleph_1 and non(N) = cof(N) = c = aleph_2 (h <= s <= non(N)), so Theorem B gives add(UN) = aleph_1. I know no independent computation of add(UN) there, and Goto has none. This is a new consequence, not cross-checked, and nothing contradicts it. The family F can be the ground-model reals: an h-slalom localising them would yield a Cohen real, which the Laver property forbids.

(iv) Width computation in Lemma 2, redone.
- Arithmetic: tau_{n-1} = tau_n + alpha_n; tau_n <= 2 alpha_{n+1} = 2^{1-4 mu_n}; (E) rho_n tau_{n-1} >= rho_n alpha_n = 2^{-2mu_n-n} >= 2^{2-4mu_n} >= 2 tau_n because 2 mu_n >= n+2. Verified exactly for n = 0..4.
- Invariant lambda(T^n(s)) >= 2 tau_{n-1}: both cases hold. It is not vacuous: lambda(E(s)) can be as small as the product of rho_m for m < n, and that product is >= 4 alpha_n >= 2 tau_{n-1} (checked exactly for n <= 4).
- Second moment: for j != j' the integrand is 1_{E_j} 1_{E_j'} (rho - 1_{R_j})(rho - 1_{R_j'}). The first factor depends only on stage-<n blocks, the other two on B_{n,k_j} and B_{n,k_j'}. These coordinate sets are pairwise disjoint because k_j != k_j'. So the three factors are independent under the product measure and the last two have mean 0. The cross term vanishes whether or not s_j = s_j'; the histories enter only through the first factor.
- Diagonal term: lambda(E_j) rho (1 - rho). Brute-force exact enumeration (4 early bits, three 2-bit blocks, random and equal E_j) confirmed the integral of Xi^2 equals the sum of lambda(E_j) rho (1 - rho) in 5 of 5 trials.
- Conclusion: N rho theta / 2 < (N rho)^{1/2}, so N < 4/(rho theta^2) = 1/(rho_n tau_{n-1}^2) <= 1/(rho_n alpha_n^2) = 2^{3 mu_n + n} = h(n). This bounds every finite subset of S(n), so |S(n)| < h(n), although S(n) quantifies over infinitely many histories.
- The point w: Q_n is closed with lambda(Q_n) >= tau_{n-1} > 0 and Q_{n+1} is a subset of Q_n. For f(n) not in S(n) the defining inequality holds for all s', in particular s' = f|n. Then w is in R_{n,f(n)} for infinitely many n, and every marker at stage n >= n_0 carries c|n. Correct.
- phi_f depends only on f and the fixed blocks, not on K or c. Lemma 3 needs this, and it holds.

Lemma 1 and the proof of Theorem B. Correct.
- Step 1 grouping gives lambda(C_n) <= eps_n and each x in G lies in infinitely many C_n; Step 2 is Borel-Cantelli.
- Injectivity of phi_f on X_f as a set of points holds: w_beta = w_beta' with f_beta = f_beta' forces c_beta = c_beta', hence beta = beta'.

(v) Corollaries.
- Goto quotes Grzegorek in exactly the form used: "there is a set X in UN of size non(N)" (Introduction, proof of Cor. 5.6(3), proof of Prop. 6.4), citing reference [6]. Grzegorek's paper itself was not checked.
- The size-b set is Goto's deduction in Cor. 5.6(2) from Reclaw's theorem that sets well-ordered by a Borel relation are UN. The note's "Reclaw: there is one of size b" should cite Goto Cor. 5.6(2). Reclaw's paper was not checked.
- non(UN) = non(N) is Goto Prop. 5.4.
- (a), (b), (c) follow as written. add(UN) <= cf(non(UN)) is the standard splitting argument.
- The "d" in (c) depends on Theorem A, which was outside my brief. I read Lemma 4 and the proof of Theorem A once and found no error (Bad has measure < (3/4) 2^{-l}; the preimage of Good under m_h is 2^omega x G).
errors: Wording only; not a gap in Theorem B or Corollaries (a)-(c). The Results sentence 'Countable support iterations of length omega_2 over CH cannot give a counterexample' is not proved as worded. Corollary (b) needs c <= aleph_2, and a countable support iteration whose iterands are large (for example a first iterand adding aleph_3 Cohen reals) gives c > aleph_2. Restrict it to iterations that force c <= aleph_2, for example proper iterands of size at most aleph_1.

attacks.summary:
I did not prove add(UN) = add(N) in the remaining case, and I did not prove add(UN) <= b or add(UN) <= cov(M). What I have is a sharper negative statement, with complete proofs.

Result: the Theorem A device needs at least cov(M) maps, whatever Borel injections and measures are used. By "the Theorem A device" I mean: a fixed set Y_f that is only assumed to have full outer measure for a fixed finite Borel measure nu_f, with the hit coming from "nu_f-positively many z have their whole leaf inside K".

Consequence for the proposed combination: with a family F of size add(N) (Lemma 2 coding plus the Theorem A device), the argument cannot work whenever add(N) < cov(M). It can only possibly work in models where add(N) = cov(M). The same device cannot prove add(UN) <= b in ZFC, since b < cov(M) is consistent; the best it could give is add(UN) <= cov(M).

The key lemma (Claim 1) is new relative to the note as far as a grep of workflow-results.json shows: fewer than cov(M) Lebesgue-singular finite Borel measures always have a common null compact set of positive Lebesgue measure. Remark 3 of the note (cov(M) <= theta_inv) is the special case of coordinate-invariant leaves.

Not excluded: schemes where the sets Z_f (size <= non(N)) are chosen by something other than full outer measure for one measure. For those I only have the trivial bound |F| >= add(N).

No file in the folder was edited. Finished about 21:10 EST. Standard facts used but not fetched: analytic sets are Lebesgue measurable; cov(M) may be computed in omega^omega; consistency of b < cov(M) (Cohen model).

claims.statement: Lemma N (common null compact set). Let cov(M) be the least number of meager subsets of omega^omega that cover omega^omega. Let |I| < cov(M). For each i in I let sigma_i be a finite Borel measure on 2^omega with sigma_i(2^omega minus G_i) = 0 for some Lebesgue-null set G_i. Let K_0 be compact with lambda(K_0) > 0. Then there is a compact K inside K_0 with lambda(K) > 0 and sigma_i(K) = 0 for every i in I.
claims.proof:
Fix the enumeration (O_k) of clopen sets from Lemma 1 of the note.

(1) By Step 1 of Lemma 1 of the note with h = 1 (so eps_n = 2^{-n}), choose f_i in omega^omega with lambda(O_{f_i(n)}) <= 2^{-n} for all n and G_i inside limsup_n O_{f_i(n)}. Put D_i(w) = {n : w in O_{f_i(n)}}. Then D_i(w) is infinite for every w in G_i, hence for sigma_i-almost every w.

(2) Choose a^i_0 < a^i_1 < ... with sigma_i{w : D_i(w) cap [a^i_j, a^i_{j+1}) is empty} <= 2^{-j}. This is possible: for fixed a, the sets E_b = {w : D_i(w) cap [a,b) is empty} are clopen and decrease in b; their intersection is inside {w : D_i(w) finite}, which is sigma_i-null; sigma_i is finite, so sigma_i(E_b) -> 0. By Borel-Cantelli the set Ex_i = {w : D_i(w) misses [a^i_j, a^i_{j+1}) for infinitely many j} is sigma_i-null.

(3) For k in omega put C_{i,k} = {g in omega^omega : for every j >= k there is n in [a^i_j, a^i_{j+1}) with g(n) != f_i(n)}. It is closed, because agreeing with f_i on a finite interval is an open condition. It is nowhere dense: given a basic open set [s], pick j >= k with a^i_j >= |s| and extend s to agree with f_i on [a^i_j, a^i_{j+1}); this gives a basic open subset of [s] disjoint from C_{i,k}. So M_i = union over k of C_{i,k} is meager. Since |I| < cov(M) there is g outside every M_i. For each i and each k there is then j >= k with g = f_i on [a^i_j, a^i_{j+1}); so this holds for infinitely many j.

(4) Choose n_0 with 2^{1-n_0} < lambda(K_0). Put g'(n) = g(n) if lambda(O_{g(n)}) <= 2^{-n}, and otherwise let g'(n) be an index of the empty set. Put U = union over n >= n_0 of O_{g'(n)}. U is open and lambda(U) <= 2^{1-n_0}. Put K = K_0 minus U. K is compact and lambda(K) > 0.

(5) Fix i and w in K. For infinitely many j with a^i_j >= n_0 we have g = f_i on [a^i_j, a^i_{j+1}). On that interval g' = g, because lambda(O_{f_i(n)}) <= 2^{-n}. Since w is not in U, w is not in O_{f_i(n)} for n in that interval, so D_i(w) misses it. Hence w is in Ex_i. So K is inside Ex_i and sigma_i(K) = 0.

claims.statement: Theorem N (the measure device needs cov(M) maps). Let |I| < cov(M). For i in I let D_i be a Borel subset of 2^omega x 2^omega, e_i : D_i -> 2^omega a Borel injection, and nu_i a finite Borel measure on 2^omega. Let P' be an uncountable subset of 2^omega (for example the Grzegorek set P, or all of 2^omega). Let K_0 be compact with lambda(K_0) > 0. Then there are a compact K inside K_0 with lambda(K) > 0 and nu_i-null Borel sets H_i such that for every i and every z outside H_i with P' x {z} inside D_i, infinitely many c in P' have e_i(c,z) not in K. In particular {z : P' x {z} inside D_i and e_i[P' x {z}] inside K} is inside H_i, so it is nu_i-null, for every i.
claims.proof:
Fix i. For c in 2^omega put Q^i_c = e_i[D_i cap ({c} x 2^omega)]. Each Q^i_c is analytic, hence Lebesgue measurable (standard fact, not fetched). The Q^i_c are pairwise disjoint for distinct c because e_i is injective. A probability measure has at most countably many pairwise disjoint measurable sets of positive measure, so lambda(Q^i_c) = 0 for all but countably many c. P' is uncountable, so choose distinct c_{i,k} in P' (k in omega) with lambda(Q^i_{c_{i,k}}) = 0.

Define sigma_{i,k}(B) = nu_i{z : (c_{i,k}, z) in D_i and e_i(c_{i,k}, z) in B} for Borel B. This is a finite Borel measure, since the section of D_i is Borel and z -> e_i(c_{i,k}, z) is Borel on it. Take a Borel null set G containing Q^i_{c_{i,k}}; then sigma_{i,k}(2^omega minus G) = 0.

The index set I x omega has size < cov(M), because cov(M) is uncountable. Apply Lemma N to the family (sigma_{i,k}) and K_0. This gives a compact K inside K_0 with lambda(K) > 0 and sigma_{i,k}(K) = 0 for all i, k.

Put H_i = union over k of {z : (c_{i,k}, z) in D_i and e_i(c_{i,k}, z) in K}. H_i is Borel and nu_i(H_i) <= sum_k sigma_{i,k}(K) = 0. If z is outside H_i and P' x {z} is inside D_i, then e_i(c_{i,k}, z) is not in K for every k; the c_{i,k} are distinct members of P'.

claims.statement: Corollary N1 (what Theorem N says about the proposed combination). Let (e_f, nu_f), f in F, be any scheme of Borel injections and finite Borel measures with |F| < cov(M). Then there is a positive-measure compact K such that, for every choice of sets Y_f, the sets Y_f' = Y_f minus H_f have the same nu_f-outer measure as Y_f and no leaf e_f[P x {z}] with z in Y_f' lies inside K. So the hypothesis 'Y_f has full nu_f-outer measure' can never be the reason that some leaf over Y_f lies in K. In particular, Lemma 2 coding combined with the Theorem A device over a family F of size add(N) cannot work if add(N) < cov(M). No argument of this form proves add(UN) <= kappa for a cardinal kappa that can consistently be below cov(M); in particular not add(UN) <= b.
claims.proof: Apply Theorem N with I = F and P' = P (P has size non(N) >= aleph_1, so it is uncountable). Removing the nu_f-null set H_f from Y_f does not change outer measure. By Theorem N, every z outside H_f whose leaf is defined has a point e_f(c,z), c in P, outside K. For the last sentence: a device with kappa maps that works in ZFC would contradict Theorem N in a model of kappa < cov(M). The consistency of b < cov(M) (Cohen model) is standard and was not fetched.
claims.confidence: high for the deduction; the consistency of b < cov(M) is quoted, not checked

claims.statement: Corollary N2. Let m be the least size of a family of Lebesgue-singular finite Borel measures on 2^omega such that every compact set of positive Lebesgue measure has positive measure for some member. Then m >= cov(M). Remark 3 of the note (cov(M) <= theta_inv) follows as a special case of Theorem N, without the Bartoszynski-Shelah theorem.
claims.proof: m >= cov(M) is Lemma N with K_0 = 2^omega. For theta_inv: let BB be a family of infinite co-infinite subsets of omega with |BB| < cov(M). For B in BB let e_B : 2^B x 2^{omega minus B} -> 2^omega be the merging homeomorphism and nu_B the product measure on 2^{omega minus B}. Identify 2^B and 2^{omega minus B} with 2^omega by the increasing enumerations of B and its complement; this identification preserves product measure. The leaves e_B[2^B x {z}] are the classes [x]_B. Theorem N with P' = 2^omega gives a positive compact K such that nu_B-almost no leaf [x]_B lies inside K. A B-invariant subset of K of positive lambda-measure would be a union of leaves over a nu_B-positive set of z (Fubini, since e_B carries lambda x nu_B to lambda). So K has no B-invariant positive subset for any B in BB, and theta_inv >= cov(M).

claims.statement: Reformulation of the Lemma 2 coding as a leaf map (used to test the idea; this is why the measure nu_f cannot be Lebesgue-like). For f in omega^omega define e_f(c,z) = the point w that equals z outside the message parts of the blocks B_{n,f(n)}, and on the message part of B_{n,f(n)} equals c|n if z has a marker at (n,f(n)) and equals z otherwise. Then e_f is continuous on 2^omega x 2^omega, and phi_f(e_f(c,z)) = c whenever z has infinitely many markers along f. For g in omega^omega the compact set K_g = {w : no marker at (n,g(n)) for n >= 1} has positive measure and contains no point with a marker at a level n >= 1 where f(n) = g(n).
claims.proof: Continuity: each coordinate of e_f(c,z) depends on finitely many coordinates of (c,z). e_f(c,z) has the same marker bits as z, so D(e_f(c,z), f) = D(z,f). If this set is infinite, every marked block B_{n,f(n)} carries message c|n, so e_f(c,z) is in dom(phi_f) and phi_f(e_f(c,z)) = c. K_g is closed. Its complement has measure <= sum_{n>=1} alpha_n = sum_{n>=1} 2^{-4^{n+1}} < 1. The last assertion is the definition of K_g. So any measure nu_f that works for f must be concentrated on the Lebesgue-null set {z : D(z,f) infinite}; this is the singular situation covered by Lemma N.

claims.statement: UNPROVED: add(UN) = add(N) when non(N) < cof(N) and every universally null set has size < cof(N). UNPROVED: add(UN) <= b. UNPROVED: add(UN) <= cov(M). UNPROVED: whether add(N) < cov(M) is compatible with the constraints of Corollary (c) of the note; I see nothing that excludes it.
claims.proof: No proof. These remain open after this attempt.

obstacles: Theorem N kills every version of the Theorem A device with fewer than cov(M) maps: any Borel injections, any finite Borel measures nu_f, and leaves taken over any uncountable code set. The reason is that fixing one code c gives a Lebesgue-singular measure for all but countably many c, and fewer than cov(M) singular measures share a null compact set of positive Lebesgue measure. So in models of add(N) < cov(M) the combination 'Lemma 2 coding + full-outer-measure set Y' is impossible with |F| = add(N).

Theorem N does not exclude schemes where Z_f (size <= non(N)) hits the sets {z : leaf_f(z) inside K} for a reason other than full outer measure for a single measure. For arbitrary Z_f I can only show the trivial bound |F| >= add(N): for each f there is a null Borel set Q_f meeting every leaf of e_f. Since |Z_f| <= non(N) < cof(N), Z_f cannot be built by recursion against a cofinal family of compact sets, so some ideal-based hitting property seems needed. A measure is the natural one and it fails.

Theorem N does not cover the weaker requirement 'for nu-positively many z, fewer than non(N) codes c in P have e(c,z) outside K' (enough for the device if Gamma is the graph of a map P -> Y with all fibres of size non(N)). The proof gives infinitely many bad codes per z, not non(N) many. Extending it to aleph_1 bad codes would use a union of aleph_1 nu-null sets and so needs add(N) > aleph_1.
In models where add(N) = cov(M) the obstruction says nothing, and the open case is not excluded there. I had no time to look for a positive construction under add(N) = cov(M).

Whether theta_inv <= cov(M) (which would give add(UN) <= cov(M) by Remark 3 of the note) was not settled. The sufficient condition used in Theorem A (the enumeration of B dominates the sequence b_K) costs d.

referee.notes:
Referee report on "zfc-remaining" (finished about 21:10 EST, deadline 21:48). No file in the folder was edited.

Verdict: no claim is false. Lemma N, Theorem N, Corollary N2 and the Reformulation check line by line. Corollary N1 has one real gap, which is fixable: Theorem N is stated for Borel injections, but the Lemma 2 leaf map e_f that N1 applies it to is not injective. Details below.

LEMMA N: correct. I checked every step.
- (1) Step 1 of Lemma 1 of the note with h = 1 does give clopen C_n with lambda(C_n) <= 2^{-n} and G_i inside limsup C_n. I re-checked that proof (grouping of cylinders, lambda(C_n) <= eps_n * sum_j 2^{-j-1}).
- (2) E_b is the complement of a finite union of clopen sets, so clopen. The E_b decrease to a subset of {D_i finite}, which is sigma_i-null. Continuity from above needs sigma_i finite, which is assumed. Borel-Cantelli applies.
- (3) C_{i,k} is closed and nowhere dense as stated. g outside every M_i agrees with f_i on infinitely many intervals.
- (4) lambda(U) <= sum_{n >= n_0} 2^{-n} = 2^{1-n_0} < lambda(K_0).
- (5) On an agreement interval beyond n_0, g' = g = f_i, so w outside U gives D_i(w) disjoint from the interval. So K is inside Ex_i.
- Independent cross-check (my own derivation): Lemma N also follows from add(E,N) >= cov(M). Take G_i Borel. By inner regularity sigma_i is concentrated on an F_sigma set F_i inside G_i, a countable union of closed null sets, so F_i is in E. Fewer than add(E,N) such sets have a null union; take open U containing it with lambda(U) < lambda(K_0) and K = K_0 minus U. So Lemma N agrees with the Bartoszynski-Shelah equality quoted in Remark 2 of the note (I did not fetch that paper myself; an earlier referee in workflow-results.json says it was fetched).
- Model tests: with Dirac measures Lemma N gives cov(M) <= non(N), which is a ZFC theorem (Rothberger). Theorem N gives cov(M) <= theta_inv <= d, consistent with Theorem A in the Cohen, random, Hechler, Laver, Mathias, Miller, Sacks and MA models, since cov(M) <= d always. No contradiction found.
- Minor: "sigma_i(2^omega minus G_i) = 0 for some Lebesgue-null set G_i" should say G_i Borel (or read the equation as outer measure). This costs nothing.

THEOREM N: correct as stated. The Q_c are analytic (in fact Borel, by injectivity), pairwise disjoint, so all but countably many are null. sigma_{i,k} is a finite Borel measure concentrated on Q_{c_{i,k}}. |I x omega| < cov(M) because cov(M) is uncountable. H_i is Borel and nu_i-null. No hidden non-measurability: every set whose measure is taken is Borel.
- Observation needed for the fix below: the proof uses injectivity only to get that the leaves Q_c are pairwise disjoint for distinct c.

COROLLARY N2: correct. m >= cov(M) is Lemma N with K_0 = 2^omega. For theta_inv I checked the measurability point: any B-invariant subset A of K equals e_B[2^B x Z] with Z inside {z : leaf inside K}, which is inside H_B. So A is inside e_B[2^B x H_B], a Borel lambda-null set. No Fubini for a non-measurable A is needed. The definition of theta_inv used matches the one in workflow-results.json ("{x : [x]_B subset K} has positive measure").

REFORMULATION claim: correct. e_f changes only message parts of blocks B_{n,f(n)}; blocks are pairwise disjoint, so all marker bits are kept and D(e_f(c,z), f) = D(z,f). Continuity and phi_f(e_f(c,z)) = c hold. {z : D(z,f) infinite} is Lebesgue null by Borel-Cantelli (sum alpha_n finite). The sentence "any nu_f that works must be concentrated on that set" is a heuristic, not a theorem; it is true in the sense that Lemma 3 (the only mechanism for universal nullness) applies only to points in dom(phi_f).

COROLLARY N1: the deduction from Theorem N is correct, but the application to the Lemma 2 coding has a gap.
- Gap. The Lemma 2 leaf map e_f on 2^omega x 2^omega is not injective. If z has no marker along f then e_f(c,z) = z for every c, and this happens for a set of z of positive Lebesgue measure. So Theorem N as stated ("Borel injection") does not apply to e_f, and the leaves Q_c are not pairwise disjoint on the full plane. The hypothesis cannot simply be dropped: for e(c,z) = z every positive compact K contains positively many (one-point) leaves.
- Fix. Restate Theorem N with the hypothesis "e_i is Borel and e_i(c,z) != e_i(c',z') whenever c != c'". The proof is unchanged. For the Lemma 2 coding take D_f = 2^omega x Z_f with Z_f = {z : D(z,f) infinite} (a G_delta set). On D_f the map phi_f decodes c, so leaves are pairwise disjoint, and each Q_c is a continuous image of a Borel set, hence analytic. Restrict nu_f to Z_f. Then N1 holds for the Lemma 2 coding. Points over z outside Z_f are outside dom(phi_f) and are useless to the device.
- Scope. Theorem N only treats z whose whole section P' x {z} lies in D_i. Schemes with partial sections are not covered; this is within the author's "not excluded" list but should be said in N1.
- The meta-statements ("cannot work if add(N) < cov(M)", "cannot prove add(UN) <= b") are correct for the device as defined: total leaves, pairwise disjoint, Y_f assumed only to have full nu_f-outer measure. They are statements about one proof method, not about add(UN).
- Not fetched by the author or by me: consistency of b < cov(M). It follows from the ZFC inequality b <= non(M) and the Cohen model (non(M) = aleph_1 < cov(M) = c); I am confident but did not check a source.

NOVELTY: overclaimed. Lemma N is a two-line corollary of add(E,N) >= cov(M) (derivation above), and workflow-results.json already contains that inequality with a self-contained proof and a referee note that it is one half of the Bartoszynski-Shelah theorem. Remark 3 of the note already says the method cannot go below cov(M) for coordinate-invariant leaves. What is new here is the extension from coordinate-invariant leaves to arbitrary disjoint-leaf Borel maps and arbitrary finite measures (Theorem N). The note should cite add(E,N) = cov(M) for Lemma N rather than call it new.

UNPROVED items: correctly marked as unproved. I found no proof or refutation of any of them.
errors: Corollary N1 / Theorem N hypothesis mismatch: Theorem N assumes e_i is a Borel injection, but the Lemma 2 leaf map e_f is not injective on 2^omega x 2^omega (e_f(c,z) = z for all c when z has no marker along f, a positive-measure set of z). Fix: weaken the hypothesis to 'e_i(c,z) != e_i(c',z') whenever c != c'' (the proof uses only disjoint leaves) and apply it on D_f = 2^omega x {z : D(z,f) infinite}, where phi_f decodes c.

Novelty overclaim: Lemma N follows in two lines from add(E,N) >= cov(M) by inner regularity (a singular finite Borel measure is concentrated on a countable union of closed null sets). That inequality is already in workflow-results.json and behind Remark 3 of the note. Only the extension to arbitrary disjoint-leaf Borel maps and measures (Theorem N) is new.
Lemma N statement: G_i should be Borel (or the equation sigma_i(2^omega minus G_i) = 0 read as outer measure). Harmless.
Corollary N1 scope: Theorem N covers only z whose whole section P' x {z} lies in D_i; schemes with partial sections are not excluded and N1 should say so.
Consistency of b < cov(M) (Cohen model, via b <= non(M)) was not fetched by the author or by this referee; standard, but unchecked.

attacks.summary:
None of the three inequalities (add(UN) <= cov(M), <= b, <= non(M)) is decided. What I have is negative: the two proposed routes cannot give anything below d. Finished 21:02 EST (deadline 21:30). All proofs below are mine, done by hand; no second referee and no formal check. No file in the folder was edited.

(a) theta_inv = d in ZFC (Claim 2). So Remark 3 of the note is not a sharpening: add(UN) <= theta_inv is the same statement as Theorem A. In the Cohen model theta_inv = d = c and in the random model theta_inv = d = aleph_1; these two values of d are standard and were not fetched.

(b) No. The "all but finitely many n" version of Lemma 2 with code-independent leaves is false in ZFC for every width h (Claim 3). Any family F of functions whose marker leaves fill a positive part of every positive compact set gives a dominating family, so |F| >= d. Closed leaves are enough for the Theorem A device as far as the device goes (it only needs a positive-measure set of u in the u-space; the union of the leaves may be null). The failure is in finding the leaves, not in using them.

(c) No proof of add(UN) <= b found. Unproved.

Extra (Claim 4): for an arbitrary family of Borel leaf maps the same random-compact-set argument gives the lower bound max(cov(M), min(d, cov(N))). So a leaf device of size cov(M) cannot exist when cov(M) < min(d, cov(N)), and a device of size b or non(M) cannot exist in the Cohen model. Whether a leaf family of size cov(M) exists when cov(N) <= cov(M) < d is not settled.

Method in all three claims: choose finite sets Z_k of strings at level g(k) at random, with summable density about k*4^-k, and let K be the reals that avoid every Z_k. A leaf with 4^k patterns below g(k) is hit by Z_k with probability about 1 - e^-k.

claims.statement: Claim 1 (finite lemma). For every k >= 1 there is N*(k) such that for every N >= N*(k) there is Z subset of 2^N with |Z| <= 2k 4^{-k} 2^N such that for every C subset of N with |C| = 2k, the number of u in 2^{N minus C} that have no extension in Z is less than e^{2-k} 2^{N-2k}.
claims.proof: Put m = 2k, p = k 4^{-k} (so 0 < p <= 1/4), q = e^{-k}, M = 2^{N-m}. Put each point of 2^N into Z independently with probability p. E|Z| = p 2^N, so by Markov P(|Z| > 2p 2^N) <= 1/2. Fix C with |C| = m. For u in 2^{N minus C} let F_u be the set of the 2^m extensions of u, and X_u = 1 if F_u is disjoint from Z, else 0. The F_u are pairwise disjoint, so the X_u are independent, and P(X_u = 1) = (1-p)^{2^m} <= exp(-p 2^m) = q. For an integer t >= 1, P(sum_u X_u >= t) <= binom(M,t) q^t <= (eMq/t)^t. Take t = ceil(e^2 q M). Then eMq/t <= 1/e, so the probability is <= e^{-t} <= exp(-e^2 q M). There are at most N^m sets C. So the probability that some C has sum_u X_u >= t is at most N^{2k} exp(-e^{2-k} 2^{N-2k}), which is < 1/2 as soon as e^{2-k} 2^{N-2k} > 2k ln N + ln 2. For fixed k the left side grows exponentially in N and the right side logarithmically, so this holds for all N >= some N*(k) (numerically N*(k) <= 4k+1 for k <= 7). For such N some Z has |Z| <= 2p 2^N and, for every C, fewer than t unhit u; since t is an integer with t < e^2 q M + 1, fewer than t means at most t-1 < e^2 q M = e^{2-k} 2^{N-2k}.

claims.statement: Claim 2 (ZFC). theta_inv = d, where theta_inv is the least size of a family BB of infinite co-infinite B subset of omega such that for every compact K with lambda(K) > 0 some B in BB has lambda{x : [x]_B subset of K} > 0. More precisely: for every g in omega^omega there is a compact K with lambda(K) >= 1/9 such that every infinite B for which K contains a B-invariant set of positive measure satisfies e_B(2k) > g(k) for all but finitely many k (e_B = increasing enumeration of B).
claims.proof: theta_inv <= d is Lemma 4 of the note with the family {ran(h) : h in D}. For >=: Let g be given. Enlarging g, assume g is strictly increasing and g(k) >= N*(k) for k >= 1 (Claim 1). For k >= 1 let Z_k subset of 2^{g(k)} be given by Claim 1 with N = g(k). Put K = {x in 2^omega : x|g(k) not in Z_k for all k >= 1}. K is closed and lambda(2^omega minus K) <= sum_{k>=1} 2k 4^{-k} = 8/9. Let B be infinite and put Good = {x : [x]_B subset of K}. Any B-invariant A subset of K is a subset of Good (x in A gives [x]_B subset of A subset of K). Suppose k >= 1 and |B cap g(k)| >= 2k. Choose C subset of B cap g(k) with |C| = 2k. Let x be such that u = x|(g(k) minus C) has an extension z in Z_k. Define y by y|g(k) = z and y(j) = x(j) for j >= g(k). Then y differs from x only on C, a subset of B, so y is in [x]_B; and y|g(k) is in Z_k, so y is not in K. So x is not in Good. Hence Good is contained in {x : x|(g(k) minus C) has no extension in Z_k}, which has measure < e^{2-k} by Claim 1. If |B cap g(k)| >= 2k for infinitely many k, then lambda(Good) = 0. So if lambda(Good) > 0, then |B cap g(k)| < 2k for all k >= some k_0; for such k the 2k numbers e_B(0),...,e_B(2k-1) are not all below g(k), so e_B(2k-1) >= g(k) and e_B(2k) > g(k). Now let BB witness theta_inv. For every g some B in BB has (k -> e_B(2k)) >=* g. So {k -> e_B(2k) : B in BB} is a dominating family and |BB| >= d.

claims.statement: Claim 3 (ZFC; answer to (b)). Use the blocks B_{n,k} and mu_n of Lemma 2 of the note. For f in omega^omega and n_0 in omega let B_{f,n_0} be the union of the B_{n,f(n)}, n >= n_0, and let m_{f,n_0}(c,u), for c in 2^omega and u in 2^{omega minus B_{f,n_0}}, be the real that equals u off B_{f,n_0} and equals 0^{mu_n} followed by c|n on B_{n,f(n)} for each n >= n_0. Call (f,n_0) leaf-good for K if the set of u with m_{f,n_0}(c,u) in K for all c has positive measure. Then for every L in omega^omega there is a compact K with lambda(K) > 1/2 such that every leaf-good (f,n_0) satisfies max_{m<=n} f(m) >= L(n) for all but finitely many n. Consequences: (i) any family F such that every positive compact K has a leaf-good (f,n_0) with f in F has |F| >= d; (ii) for every width h there is a positive compact K such that for every slalom S of width h there is f with f(n) not in S(n) for all n and (f,n_0) not leaf-good for any n_0. So the 'all but finitely many' form of Lemma 2 with code-independent leaves is false.
claims.proof: Fix L and n >= 1. For L' >= L(n) let Lambda = Lambda_n be the union of the blocks B_{m,k}, m <= n, k < L'; |Lambda| tends to infinity with L'. A pattern is a pair (n_0, sigma) with n_0 <= n and sigma a function from [n_0,n] to L(n); there are at most (n+1) L(n)^{n+1} patterns. For a pattern put C_sigma = union of B_{m,sigma(m)}, n_0 <= m <= n, and for u in 2^{Lambda minus C_sigma} and tau in 2^n let z_{u,tau} in 2^Lambda equal u off C_sigma and 0^{mu_m} followed by tau|m on B_{m,sigma(m)}. Let F_{sigma,u} = {z_{u,tau} : tau in 2^n}; it has 2^n elements (the block at level n carries tau), and for fixed sigma the sets F_{sigma,u} are pairwise disjoint. Choose Z subset of 2^Lambda at random with probability p = n 2^{-n} per point. As in Claim 1: P(F_{sigma,u} misses Z) = (1-p)^{2^n} <= e^{-n}; for a fixed pattern these events are independent over the M = 2^{|Lambda|-|C_sigma|} values of u; the probability that at least ceil(e^{2-n} M) of them occur is <= exp(-e^{2-n} M); and M >= 2^{|Lambda| - sum_{m<=n}(mu_m+m)}. Choose L' so large that (n+1) L(n)^{n+1} exp(-e^{2-n} 2^{|Lambda| - sum_{m<=n}(mu_m+m)}) < 1/2. With Markov for |Z| this gives Z_n subset of 2^{Lambda_n} with |Z_n| <= 2n 2^{-n} 2^{|Lambda_n|} such that for every pattern fewer than e^{2-n} M of the u have F_{sigma,u} disjoint from Z_n. Put K = {x : x|Lambda_n not in Z_n for all n >= 6}. K is closed and lambda(complement) <= sum_{n>=6} 2n 2^{-n} = 7/16. Let (f,n_0) be given and let n >= max(n_0,6) satisfy f(m) < L(n) for all m <= n. Put sigma = f|[n_0,n]. Blocks are pairwise disjoint and Lambda_n is a union of blocks of levels <= n, so Lambda_n cap B_{f,n_0} = C_sigma. For u' in 2^{omega minus B_{f,n_0}} put u = u'|(Lambda_n minus C_sigma); u is uniformly distributed. If F_{sigma,u} meets Z_n, say z_{u,tau} in Z_n, then for any c extending tau, m_{f,n_0}(c,u')|Lambda_n = z_{u,tau} is in Z_n, so m_{f,n_0}(c,u') is not in K. So {u' : m_{f,n_0}(c,u') in K for all c} has measure < e^{2-n}. If there are infinitely many such n the measure is 0 and (f,n_0) is not leaf-good. This proves the main statement. (i) If F is as stated, then for every L some f in F has (n -> max_{m<=n} f(m)) >=* L, so these functions form a dominating family and |F| >= d. (ii) Given h take L(n) = 1 + max_{m<=n} h(m) and K as above. Given S of width h let f(n) = min(omega minus S(n)) <= h(n). Then max_{m<=n} f(m) < L(n) for every n, so (f,n_0) is not leaf-good for any n_0.

claims.statement: Claim 4 (ZFC; general leaf devices). Let (U,nu) be a Polish space with a Borel probability measure and MM a family of Borel maps m : 2^omega x U -> 2^omega such that for nu-almost every u the leaf leaf_u = {m(c,u) : c in 2^omega} is infinite. Suppose for every compact K with lambda(K) > 0 some m in MM has nu{u : leaf_u subset of K} > 0. Then |MM| >= min(d, max(cov(M), cov(N))) = max(cov(M), min(d, cov(N))). The same holds if codes are restricted to a fixed subset of 2^omega, as long as almost every restricted leaf is infinite.
claims.proof: For m in MM, k >= 1, let s_{m,u}(k) be the least N such that {y|N : y in leaf_u} has at least 4^k elements; it is finite when leaf_u is infinite. The sets {u : t in leaf_u|N} are analytic, hence nu-measurable, so u -> s_{m,u}(k) is nu-measurable. Choose h_m(k) with nu{u : s_{m,u}(k) <= h_m(k)} >= 1 - 2^{-k}. Assume |MM| < d. Then there is a strictly increasing g such that for every m in MM, g(k) > h_m(k) for infinitely many k. Put p_k = k 4^{-k}. Let ZZ_k be the set of Z subset of 2^{g(k)} with |Z| <= 2 p_k 2^{g(k)}, with the measure P_k obtained from the Bernoulli(p_k) product by conditioning on ZZ_k (the condition has probability >= 1/2). Let ZZ be the product of the ZZ_k (k >= 1) with the product measure P; ZZ is a product of finite sets with at least two points each, so it is homeomorphic to Cantor space, and P is an atomless Borel probability measure, so its null ideal has covering number cov(N). For Z in ZZ put K_Z = {x : x|g(k) not in Z_k for all k >= 1}; it is closed and lambda(K_Z) >= 1 - 8/9. Fix m. For k with g(k) > h_m(k) let A_k(Z_k) = {u : leaf_u|g(k) is disjoint from Z_k}; note {u : leaf_u subset of K_Z} is a subset of A_k(Z_k). If s_{m,u}(k) <= g(k), then leaf_u|g(k) has at least 4^k points and P_k(Z_k misses it) <= 2(1-p_k)^{4^k} <= 2e^{-k}. By Fubini (ZZ_k is finite) the P_k-mean of nu(A_k(Z_k)) is <= 2e^{-k} + 2^{-k} =: eps_k. Measure: the P-mean of nu{u : leaf_u subset of K_Z} is <= eps_k for infinitely many k, so it is 0, so R_m = {Z : nu{u : leaf_u subset of K_Z} > 0} is P-null. Category: for eps > 0 the set O_eps of Z such that nu(A_k(Z_k)) < eps for some k with g(k) > h_m(k) is open (each condition depends on one coordinate) and dense (given a finite part of Z, pick such a k beyond it with eps_k < eps and a Z_k with nu(A_k(Z_k)) <= eps_k). R_m is disjoint from the intersection of the O_{1/j}, so R_m is meager. If |MM| < cov(N) or |MM| < cov(M), some Z lies in no R_m; then K_Z is a positive compact set for which no m in MM works, a contradiction. So |MM| >= d, or |MM| >= cov(N) and |MM| >= cov(M). The two forms of the bound agree because cov(M) <= d. For restricted codes the proof is the same.

Referee report on "covM-bound". Finished 21:07 EST (deadline 21:48). I read add-UN-note.md in full and checked every step by hand. I ran one short script for the arithmetic. No file in the folder was edited. Nothing was fetched from the web.

VERDICT: Claims 1, 2 and 3 are correct as written. Claim 4 is correct in its main form but has two gaps; both are repaired below. Claim 5 is correct; its unfetched consistency fact can be replaced by a short standard argument (below, from memory, not fetched). I found no wrong inequality direction and no model that contradicts any claim.

CLAIM 1: correct.
- p = k 4^-k <= 1/4. (1-p)^(4^k) <= e^-k. The F_u are disjoint for fixed C, so the X_u are independent.
- P(sum >= t) <= binom(M,t) q^t <= (eMq/t)^t <= e^-t with t = ceil(e^2 q M) >= 1. The union bound over at most N^(2k) sets C is right.
- Markov gives P(|Z| > 2p 2^N) <= 1/2 and the other event has probability < 1/2, so a good Z exists.
- "Fewer than t" gives at most t-1 < e^2 q M. Correct.
- Script check: e^(2-k) 2^(N-2k) > 2k ln N + ln 2 holds for k <= 7 and 4k+1 <= N < 4k+200.

CLAIM 2 (theta_inv = d): correct.
- The claim's definition of theta_inv agrees with Remark 3 of the note. The set Good = {x : [x]_B subset of K} is closed, and every B-invariant subset of K lies in Good.
- Upper bound: Lemma 4 of the note with {ran(h) : h in D}. Checked.
- Lower bound: sum 2k 4^-k = 8/9, so lambda(K) >= 1/9. The point y (equal to z below g(k), equal to x above) differs from x only on C, a subset of B. So x is not in Good. The measure bound e^(2-k) follows from Claim 1.
- |B cap g(k)| < 2k gives e_B(2k-1) >= g(k). Dominating the enlarged g dominates the original g.
- So Remark 3 of the note gives nothing beyond Theorem A. The note's line "cov(M) <= theta_inv <= d" is true but not sharp.

CLAIM 3: correct for the leaf as defined (markers at every level n >= n_0).
- The set {u : m(c,u) in K for all c} is closed, so there is no measurability problem.
- Pattern count <= (n+1) L(n)^(n+1). |F_{sigma,u}| = 2^n because level n is in [n_0,n]. The F_{sigma,u} are disjoint for fixed sigma. p = n 2^-n <= 1/2.
- sum_{n>=6} 2n 2^-n = 7/16, so lambda(K) >= 9/16.
- Lambda_n cap B_{f,n_0} = C_sigma holds because blocks are pairwise disjoint and f(m) < L(n) <= L'.
- (i) and (ii) follow. (ii) refutes exactly this statement: "there is h such that for every K there is a slalom S of width h such that every f with f(n) not in S(n) for almost all n is leaf-good for some n_0".
- Scope remark (mine, quick proof, not double-checked). The claim does not cover leaves that put markers only on an infinite set D of levels. The same proof extends. Use patterns (E, sigma) with E a subset of n+1, n in E, sigma : E -> L(n). There are at most 2^n max(L(n),1)^(n+1) of them. For L nondecreasing, leaf-good (f,D) then gives max{f(m) : m in D, m <= n} >= L(n) for all but finitely many n in D. So F_{f,D}(n) = max{f(m) : m in D, m <= min(D minus n)} dominates L. Hence the number of pairs (f,D) is >= d. The number of functions f alone need not be >= d, but the device uses one universally null set per pair.

CLAIM 4: main statement correct after one small repair; the restricted-codes extension needs a second repair.
- Gap 1 (trivial). g must also satisfy g(k) >= 2k+1. Otherwise ZZ_k can be {emptyset} for all large k (example g(k) = k: 2 p_k 2^g(k) < 1 for k >= 4). Then ZZ is finite and the cov(N), cov(M) arguments fail. With g(k) >= 2k+1, ZZ_k contains emptyset and all singletons. Every point mass of P_k is at most 2(1-p_k)^(2^g(k)) <= 2 e^(-2k), so P is atomless and ZZ is perfect. Enlarging g keeps "g(k) > h_m(k) for infinitely many k".
- Measure step. The claim uses the P-mean of nu{u : leaf_u subset of K_Z} without showing this is measurable in Z. It is (the set of pairs (Z,u) is coanalytic). A cleaner route: phi(Z) = inf over the relevant k of nu(A_k(Z_k)) is Borel, bounds nu{u : leaf_u subset of K_Z} from above, and has mean <= eps_k for infinitely many k. So phi = 0 almost surely and R_m lies in a Borel P-null set.
- Category step: checked. O_eps is open and dense. R_m is disjoint from the intersection of the O_(1/j).
- Conditioning costs a factor 2: P_k(miss) <= 2(1-p_k)^(4^k) <= 2 e^-k. Correct. The identity min(d, max(cov(M),cov(N))) = max(cov(M), min(d,cov(N))) is correct because cov(M) <= d.
- The hypothesis "almost every leaf is infinite" is needed. The map m(c,u) = u alone would satisfy the rest.
- Gap 2 (hidden non-measurability). "The same holds if codes are restricted to a fixed subset E" is proved only when E is analytic. In the intended use E is a universally null set, which is not analytic. Then {u : |leaf_u|N| >= 4^k} and {u : leaf_u subset of K} can be non-measurable. "nu{...} > 0" is then undefined, and the choice of h_m and the Fubini step fail as written.
- Repair of Gap 2 (my proof). State the hypothesis with inner measure: nu_*{u : leaf_u subset of K} > 0. This is the reading the device needs, since a fixed set Y of full outer measure must meet the set. Put T_N = {u : |leaf_u|N| >= 4^k}. These increase with N and their union has full outer measure. Outer measure is continuous along increasing unions, so choose h_m(k) with nu^*(T_{h_m(k)}) >= 1 - 2^-k. For each Z in ZZ_k take a Borel G_Z inside A_k(Z) with nu(G_Z) = nu_*(A_k(Z)). The function psi(u) = P_k{Z : u in G_Z} is Borel and psi <= 2e^-k on T_{g(k)}. So {psi > 2e^-k} is a Borel set disjoint from T_{h_m(k)} and has measure <= 2^-k. Hence the P_k-mean of nu_*(A_k(Z)) is <= eps_k. The rest is unchanged with nu_* in place of nu. With outer measure in the hypothesis the statement is unproved.

CLAIM 5: correct, given the following.
- (i) is Claim 2. (ii) is Claim 3(i); it needs a model of cov(M) < d, for example the Laver or Miller model (standard, not fetched).
- (iii) Cohen model: b = non(M) = aleph_1 < cov(M) = c = aleph_2. Standard, from memory, not fetched.
- (iii) Consistency of cov(M) < min(d, cov(N)). The agent's guess (countable support iteration of random and Laver forcing) is not needed. Simpler argument, from standard facts recalled from memory, not fetched: start with MA + c = aleph_2 and add aleph_2 random reals with the measure algebra. Then cov(N) = aleph_2, because every aleph_1 null sets are coded in a submodel missing one random real. non(N) = aleph_1, because aleph_1 of the random reals form a non-null set. So cov(M) <= non(N) = aleph_1 (Rothberger). d stays aleph_2, because the forcing is ccc and omega^omega-bounding and d = aleph_2 in the ground model.
- (iv) is an honest "undecided". I found no proof or counter-model either.

SUMMARY CHECK. (a) and (b) of the summary are supported by Claims 2 and 3. The remark that closed leaves suffice for the Theorem A device is right: m_{f,n_0} is continuous and injective on a compact space, so m[Gamma] is universally null, and the set of good u is closed. The image of m is null, which does no harm.

attacks.summary:
Finished 21:04 EST (deadline 21:30). No file in the folder was edited.

RESULT. None of the standard constructions I checked is a plausible model of add(N) < add(UN). Each one fails for one of three reasons:
(1) the numerical constraints of the note (Theorems A, B),
(2) Goto's Theorem 5.18 applied with theta = the intended value of add(N),
(3) a transfer of Goto's Tukey connection through the "intersection with a sigma-closed model" step (Proposition C below: my adaptation of Lemma 7.3 of Brendle-Cardona-Mejia arXiv:2309.01931, written in full, not refereed).
Still unchecked: the Boolean-ultrapower versions, the alternative-order Cichon's maximum (its initial forcing uses the Kellner-Shelah-Tanasie poset E-tilde), and Brendle's shattered iterations.

SOURCES FETCHED (titles, authors and values read from arXiv pages or PDF text):
- arXiv:1708.03691, "Cichon's maximum", Goldstern, Kellner, Shelah. Abstract: aleph_1 < add(N) < cov(N) < b < non(M) < cov(M) < d < non(N) < cof(N) < c, from four strongly compact cardinals.
- arXiv:1906.06608, "Cichon's maximum without large cardinals", Goldstern, Kellner, Mejia, Shelah. Theorem 3.1: add(N)=mu_1 <= cov(N)=mu_2 <= b=mu_3 <= non(M)=mu_4 <= cov(M)=mu_5 <= d=mu_6 <= non(N)=mu_7 <= cof(N)=mu_8 <= c=mu_9. Theorem 4.1: add(N) <= b <= cov(N) <= non(M) <= cov(M) <= non(N) <= d <= cof(N) <= c. Both use P^fin = P^pre intersected with a sigma-closed model. Theorem 2.4 (P^pre): add(N)=mu_1 < cov(N)=mu_2 < b=mu_3 < non(M)=mu_4 < cov(M)=c.

- arXiv:1809.05004, "Filter-linkedness and its effect on preservation of cardinal characteristics", Brendle, Cardona, Mejia. Theorem B (5.3): add(N)=theta_0 <= cov(N)=theta_1 <= b=theta_2 <= non(M)=mu <= cov(M)=nu <= d=non(N)=c=lambda. Theorem D (5.4): add(N)=theta_0 <= b=theta_1 <= cov(N)=non(M)=mu <= cov(M)=non(N)=nu <= d=c=lambda. Theorem F (5.7): the 1708.03691 ordering from three strongly compacts. The text also says E is sigma-centered.
- arXiv:2309.01931, "Separating cardinal characteristics of the strong measure zero ideal", Brendle, Cardona, Mejia (Goto's reference [3]). Theorems 5.8, 5.10, 6.9, 7.1, Lemmas 3.5, 7.2, 7.3, Corollary 5.9 read.

- arXiv:2302.05069, "Shattered Iterations", Brendle. Only the abstract (aleph_1 < cov(M) < non(M)) and a search snippet were read.

VERDICT PER CONSTRUCTION
- Creature forcing (Fischer-Goldstern-Kellner-Shelah, both orders): d = aleph_1, so Theorem A gives add(UN) = add(N) = aleph_1. Dead. arXiv:2309.01931 Section 8 says the decisive-creature method is restricted to omega^omega-bounding forcings (d = aleph_1), so the whole family is dead.
- Left-side models with cov(M) = c or non(N) = c: dead by Corollary (a). These are Theorem 2.4 of 1906.06608, result (i) of 1712.00778, Theorem B of 1809.05004, Theorem 6.9 of 2309.01931, Goto's Corollary 5.19 model, and Mejia's Theorems 2, 3, 5, 20, 21.
- Mejia Theorems 11, 12, 14 (non(N) = cof(N)) and 13, 15 (add(N) = non(N)): dead numerically.
- Mejia Theorems 4, 6, 16-19 and Theorem D of 1809.05004: these pass every numerical constraint. They are finite support iterations whose iterands are small posets (size < value of add(N)), random subalgebras and sigma-centered posets. Goto's Theorem 5.18 with theta = value of add(N) gives add(UN) <= add(SN,N) <= add(N). Dead, modulo the hypothesis checks listed in Claim 2.
- Cichon's maximum by the submodel method (2309.01931 Theorem 7.1; 1906.06608 Theorem 3.1): passes every numerical constraint and is not literally an iteration covered by 5.18. Proposition C transfers Goto's Tukey connection to P intersect N and gives add(SN,N) <= add(N). Dead if Proposition C is right. It is fully worked out for Theorem 7.1 of 2309.01931; for Theorem 3.1 of 1906.06608 one more check is needed (Claim 4).
- Cichon's maximum by Boolean ultrapowers (1708.03691; 1809.05004 Theorem F): passes the numerical constraints. NOT settled here. 2309.01931 Section 8 says the S^f connection transfers under Boolean ultrapowers; the analogue for (SN, N) is unproved.
- Alternative order (1712.00778 (ii); 1906.06608 Theorem 4.1): passes the numerical constraints. NOT settled. I did not read the iterands of its initial forcing and do not know if E-tilde is R^pt-good.
- Shattered iterations (2302.05069): not a finite support iteration, d >= cov(M) > aleph_1, c >= aleph_3. NOT settled; its values of add(N), b, cof(N) were not fetched. This is the only construction on the list to which none of the three arguments applies.

WHAT A SURVIVOR WOULD NEED
(a) Every universally null set has size < cof(N). In particular no set of size cof(N) is well-ordered by a Borel relation, for example no <*-increasing sequence of ordinal length >= cof(N).
(b) Every union of add(N) universally null sets is Lebesgue null (Goto: add(UN) = add(UN, N)).
(c) By 5.18, the forcing must use iterands that are not theta-R^pt-good for theta = add(N): posets of size >= add(N) with no strictly positive finitely additive measure, which do not raise add(N) but make unions of add(N) strong-measure-zero sets null. No construction on the list has such iterands.

Numerical part: in each listed model add(N) < non(N) < cof(N) = c, add(N) < d, b < cof(N) and non(N) is regular and larger than add(N), once the parameters are chosen strictly increasing. For Theorem 4 and Theorem D, cof(N) = c follows from d = c. So c >= aleph_3 is possible and no constraint fails.

(2) Posets of size < theta are theta-R-good for regular theta: Lemma 3.5 of arXiv:2309.01931, citing [CM19, Lemma 4.10]. claims.statement: Proposition C (transfer through a sigma-closed model; adaptation of Lemma 7.3 of arXiv:2309.01931, not refereed). Let chi be large and regular, N an elementary submodel of H_chi closed under countable sequences, P in N a ccc poset, and theta in N an uncountable regular cardinal. Suppose P forces: there are strong measure zero sets X_beta (beta < theta) such that for every null set G the set {beta < theta : X_beta is a subset of G} is bounded in theta. Then P intersect N forces add(SN, N) <= cf(sup(theta intersect N)), hence add(UN) <= cf(sup(theta intersect N)).
claims.proof:
Quoted from arXiv:2309.01931, Section 7 (read in the PDF text): (Q1) P intersect N is a complete subposet of P and is ccc. (Q2) Nice P intersect N-names of reals correspond to nice P-names of reals that lie in N. (Q3) For p in P intersect N, a sufficiently absolute formula phi and P-names tau in N of members of H_{aleph_1}: p forces_P phi(tau) iff p forces_{P intersect N} phi(tau). (Q4) If Core is a P-core of the increasing functions (a set of nice P-names such that every P-name of an increasing function is forced equal to exactly one member), then Core intersect N is a P intersect N-core. (Q5) A nice P-name of a member of SN is a sequence sigma = <sigma^f : f in Core> with sigma^f a nice name of a member of prod_n 2^{f(n)}; it names the set X = intersection over f of [sigma^f]_infinity, where [s]_infinity = {x : s(n) is an initial segment of x for infinitely many n}; this set is in SN.

Step 0 (normal form). Given X_beta as in the hypothesis, for each beta and each f in Core pick a name sigma_beta^f for a member of prod_n 2^{f(n)} with X_beta a subset of the union of the [sigma_beta^f(n)], and replace X_beta by Y_beta = intersection over f of [sigma_beta^f]_infinity when X_beta already has this form, as it does in Goto's proof of 5.18. There X_beta = intersection over alpha in Z_beta of [sigma_alpha]_infinity and {f_alpha : alpha in Z_beta} is the set of all increasing functions; put sigma_beta^f = sigma_alpha for the least alpha in Z_beta with f_alpha = f. Then Y_beta contains X_beta, Y_beta is in SN, and Y_beta not a subset of G whenever X_beta is not. So we may assume the hypothesis holds for a sequence <sigma_beta : beta < theta> of nice P-names of SN members. The statement that such a sequence exists holds in H_chi with parameters P, theta in N, so by elementarity we may take the sequence in N.

Step 1. Let p in P intersect N and let tau be a nice P intersect N-name of a Borel code of a null G_delta set G_tau. By (Q2) tau is a P-name in N. The hypothesis gives, in H_chi: there are q <= p and b < theta such that for all beta with b < beta < theta, q forces_P 'Y_beta is not a subset of G_tau' (extend p to decide a bound b; this uses that theta is a ground model ordinal). By elementarity take q and b in N.

Step 2. Fix beta in theta intersect N with beta > b. Then q forces_P 'there is x in Y_beta minus G_tau'. By the maximum principle and elementarity there is a nice P-name x in N of a real with q forces_P 'x in Y_beta and x not in G_tau'. For each f in Core intersect N the name sigma_beta^f is in N and q forces_P 'x in [sigma_beta^f]_infinity'. This is an arithmetical statement about reals with names in N, so by (Q3) q forces_{P intersect N} 'x in [sigma_beta^f]_infinity'. Also by (Q3) q forces_{P intersect N} 'x not in G_tau'.

Step 3. By (Q4) and (Q5), sigma_beta restricted to Core intersect N is a nice P intersect N-name of the SN set Y'_beta = intersection over f in Core intersect N of [sigma_beta^f]_infinity, and in the P intersect N-extension every increasing function is the value of some f in Core intersect N. By Step 2, q forces_{P intersect N} 'x in Y'_beta minus G_tau'. So q forces_{P intersect N}: for every beta in theta intersect N above b, Y'_beta is not a subset of G_tau.

Step 4. Since p and tau were arbitrary and every null set is contained in a null G_delta set, P intersect N forces: for every null G there is b in theta intersect N such that Y'_beta is not a subset of G for all beta in theta intersect N above b. Let C be a cofinal subset of theta intersect N of order type cf(sup(theta intersect N)); theta intersect N has no largest element by elementarity. If the union of the Y'_beta, beta in C, were contained in a null G, take b for G and beta in C above b: contradiction. So |C| strong measure zero sets have a non-null union, and add(SN, N) <= |C|. Finally add(UN) = add(UN, N) <= add(SN, N) because SN is a subset of UN (Goto, Section 5.6). QED.

The proof follows the proof of Lemma 7.3(a) of 2309.01931 line by line; the only change is that the relation 'A is a subset of the union of the [tau(i)]' is replaced by 'A is a subset of the null set coded by tau', and both are refuted by a single real with an absolute property.

claims.statement: Claim 4 (Cichon's maximum by the submodel method). (a) In the Cichon's maximum model of Theorem 7.1 of arXiv:2309.01931 (add(N) = add(SN) = lambda^b_1 <= cov(N) <= cov(SN) <= b <= non(M) <= cov(M) <= d <= non(SN) <= non(N) <= cof(N) <= c), add(UN) = add(N), given Goto's Theorem 5.18 and Proposition C. (b) The same conclusion holds for Theorem 3.1 of arXiv:1906.06608 provided the iterands of its initial forcing P^pre are theta-R^pt-good for theta = the P^pre-value of add(N); this proviso is NOT checked.
claims.proof:
(a) The model is P intersect N, where P is the poset of Theorem 6.9 of 2309.01931 and N is sigma-closed. P is the finite support iteration <P_{theta_6, xi}, Q_{theta_6, xi} : xi < pi> with pi = theta_6.theta_6.theta_5 (stated in the proof of 6.9). The proof of 6.9(b) lists the iterands and their goodness: Cohen and E of intermediate models (sigma-centered, Corollary 5.9(iii)), LOC^N with |N| < theta_1 (Lemma 3.5), B^N (random subalgebras, Corollary 5.9(i)), (E_b)^N (Corollary 5.9(ii), these carry strictly positive finitely additive measures by Theorem 5.8 and Lemma 5.5), D^N (sigma-centered). By Goto's Theorem 5.17 the posets with such measures and the sigma-centered ones are R^pt-good, and posets of size < theta_1 are theta_1-good. So Goto's Theorem 5.18 applies with theta_0 = aleph_1, theta = theta_1, lambda = theta_6 = theta_6^{aleph_0}, delta = theta_6.theta_5, cf(pi) = theta_5: P forces that sets X_beta (beta < theta_6) in SN exist with |{beta : X_beta subset of G}| < theta_1 for every null G. Restricting to beta < theta_1 gives the hypothesis of Proposition C with theta = theta_1. In the proof of Theorem 7.1, N is chosen with lambda^b_1 Tukey-below S_1 intersect N and add(N) = lambda^b_1 forced by P intersect N through the linear witness of length theta_1; this is the statement cf(sup(theta_1 intersect N)) = lambda^b_1. I did not verify this last equality from the construction of N in [CM22, Sec. 5]; I infer it from item (b') in the proof of Theorem 7.1 (lambda^b_i Tukey-below S_i intersect N) together with the forced value add(N) = lambda^b_1. If instead one uses the directed system S_1 = [theta_6]^{<theta_1} intersect V in place of the linear order theta_1, the proof of Proposition C goes through unchanged with 'b in S_1 intersect N' and 'beta not in b', and item (b') then gives add(SN, N) <= b(S_1 intersect N) <= lambda^b_1 directly. Hence add(N) <= add(UN) <= add(SN,N) <= lambda^b_1 = add(N).
(b) Same argument with P^pre of Theorem 2.4 of 1906.06608 (proved in arXiv:1708.03691). Its iterands are described in the literature as partial amoeba, partial random, partial Hechler and partial E forcings; 1809.05004 states that E is sigma-centered. I did not read the definition of P^pre, in particular not the size bound on the partial amoeba posets. Unproved until that is read.

(iii): the fetched abstract gives only aleph_1 < cov(M) < non(M); a search snippet reports a ccc extension with cov(M) = non(N) = kappa and cov(N) = non(M) = lambda, and 2309.01931 says the method gives add(N) < non(N) < cov(N) < cof(N). The values of add(N), b and cof(N) were not fetched. The poset is not a finite support iteration, d >= cov(M) > aleph_1, and c >= aleph_3, so nothing in the note or in 5.18 applies.

claims.statement: Claim 6 (the 'selector' form of Theorem B gives nothing new). Let sel be the least size of a family K of compact sets of positive measure such that every set meeting all members of K is non-null. The proof of Theorem B shows: a universally null set of size sel implies add(UN) = add(N). But sel = cof(N) in ZFC.
claims.proof: The proof of Theorem B uses the cofinal family only through the fact that {w_beta} meets every K_beta and is therefore non-null, so it works for any family K as above. sel <= cof(N): the family {K_beta} in the note's proof. sel >= cof(N): let K be such a family and Q the countable group of finite-support elements of 2^omega. For K in the family put U_K = complement of K (open, measure < 1) and U*_K = intersection over q in Q of (U_K + q). U*_K is Borel, Q-invariant and has measure <= measure(U_K) < 1, so it is null by the Kolmogorov 0-1 law. Let G be null. Then G + Q is null, so it misses some K in the family, that is G + Q is a subset of U_K. As G + Q is Q-invariant, G + Q is a subset of U_K + q for every q, so G is a subset of U*_K. Thus {U*_K} is a cofinal family of null sets and |K| >= cof(N).

OVERALL. Claims 1, 2, 6 and Proposition C hold. Claim 4(a) has a wrong step in its fallback argument and an invalid inference in its main argument; the conclusion is rescued by the repair below. Claims 4(b) and 5 are honestly marked unproved. Everything in Claims 2-4 depends on Goto's Theorems 5.17 and 5.18 (arXiv preprint, not refereed); I read the proof of 5.18 in flat.txt and found no error, but did not check its use of [BCM, Lemma 4.8, Theorem 4.9].

WHAT I CHECKED MYSELF
- Citations: arXiv API fetched for 1402.0367, 1708.03691, 1712.00778, 1809.05004, 1906.06608, 1211.5209, 2309.01931, 2302.05069. Titles, authors and abstract chains match the report. (1712.00778 also has add(M) = b; harmless.)
- Values read in the text extractions: Mejia Thms 2-6, 11-21; BCM-filter Thms 5.3, 5.4; BCM-SN Thm 6.9, 7.1; GKMS Thm 2.4. All match Claim 1 and Claim 2.
- BCM-SN line 2889: the decisive-creature method "is restricted to omega^omega-bounding forcings". Matches.

CLAIM 1: sound, given the note. Each case reduces to d = aleph_1 (Theorem A), non(N) = cof(N) (Corollary (a)), or add(N) = non(N) (add(N) <= add(UN) <= non(N)). The inequalities go the right way.

CLAIM 2: sound, and I closed most of the items the agent left open.
- BCM-SN Lemma 3.5 is stated for an arbitrary generalized Polish relational system ("for the rest of this section fix a gPrs R"). So posets of size < theta are theta-R^pt-good.
- Mejia Thm 6, third iterand (read): finite support product of lambda subalgebras of amoeba of size < mu_1. Good.
- Mejia Thms 16-19 (read): iterands are B^{V_{t,xi}}, D^{V_{t,xi}}, full E, D or B, and suborders of amoeba of size < mu_1. Restricted random algebras carry Lebesgue measure as a pfam; restricted and full Hechler and E are sigma-centered; the rest are small. All are mu_1-R^pt-good. The top row is a finite support iteration of length kappa + lambda.kappa.nu = lambda.(kappa.nu), cofinality nu.
- lambda^{aleph_0} = lambda in the intermediate model: Mejia's GCH_lambda gives 2^{aleph_0} = lambda because cf(lambda) >= mu_1 > aleph_0.
- Subalgebras of a sigma-centered Boolean algebra are sigma-centered (intersect the centered pieces).
Small defects, harmless: (i) the poset of BCM-filter Thm 5.4 is H_{theta_1} * C_lambda * P; the report describes only P. Apply 5.18 in V^{H*C_lambda}, where lambda^{aleph_0} = lambda still holds. (ii) 5.18 needs nontrivial iterands; "all subalgebras of size < mu_1" includes the trivial one. Drop trivial factors from the products. (iii) The citation for (E_b^h)^N is garbled: BCM Lemma 5.5(ii) gives the pfam, Theorem 5.8 gives goodness. I did not read Lemma 2.18, which links E_b^h to B_b^h.

PROPOSITION C: sound. I checked each step.
- P intersect N is a complete suborder of P (ccc plus sigma-closed N). Nice names of reals for P intersect N are countable, so they lie in N and are P-names.
- For q in P intersect N and an absolute statement about such names, q forces it in P iff q forces it in P intersect N (extend a P intersect N-generic to a P-generic).
- Steps 1-4 are correct. The bound b can be decided because theta is a ground-model ordinal. theta intersect N has no largest element.
Repair needed in Step 0 only. As written it picks sigma_beta^f with X_beta inside the union of the [sigma_beta^f(n)]; then Y_beta need not contain X_beta. Use covers "infinitely often": every strong measure zero set X has, for each increasing f, some sigma in prod 2^{f(n)} with X inside [sigma]_infinity. Then Y_beta contains X_beta, Y_beta is in SN, and {beta : Y_beta inside G} is inside {beta : X_beta inside G}. For Goto's sets, "the least alpha in Z_beta with f_alpha = f" is not decided in the ground model; sigma_beta^f must be the mixed name. Neither point affects the result.

CLAIM 4(a): the conclusion holds, but not by the written proof.
Error 1 (main route). The equality cf(sup(theta_1 intersect N)) = lambda^b_1 is not verified, and the stated inference is invalid. Proposition C plus add(N) = lambda^b_1 gives only cf(sup(theta_1 intersect N)) >= lambda^b_1. Item (b') is about the directed set S_1 intersect N, not about the linear order theta_1 intersect N.
Error 2 (fallback route). The transfer with "b in S_1 intersect N, beta not in b" gives (theta_6 intersect N, S_1 intersect N, in) Tukey-below (SN, N, subset). Item (b') bounds b(S_1 intersect N, subset), and b(S_1 intersect N, subset) <= b(theta_6 intersect N, S_1 intersect N, in) (map beta to {beta}). This is the wrong direction. An unbounded family {s_i : i < lambda^b_1} gives the uncovered point set union of (s_i intersect N), which can have size up to lambda > lambda^b_1.
Repair (complete proof). Theorem 6.9 assumes cof([theta_6]^{<theta_1}) = theta_6. Fix in N a cofinal family {a_xi : xi < theta_6} of S_1 = [theta_6]^{<theta_1} intersect V and phi : S_1 -> theta_6 with a inside a_{phi(a)}. Let X_beta (beta < theta_6) be Goto's sets from 5.18 with theta = theta_1, and put Y_a = Y_{phi(a)} (the normal form of X_{phi(a)}). P forces: for every null G the set B_G = {beta : X_beta inside G} has size < theta_1, so the union of the a_xi (xi in B_G) has size < theta_1 and, by ccc, lies inside some b in S_1. If Y_a is inside G then phi(a) is in B_G, so a is inside b. So P forces: for every null G there is b in S_1 such that Y_a is not inside G for every a in S_1 not inside b. Now run Steps 1-4 of Proposition C with index set S_1 and "a not inside b" in place of "beta > b"; they go through word for word (b is a ground-model object, so a condition decides it). Result: P intersect N forces that for every null G there is b in S_1 intersect N with Y'_a not inside G for all a in S_1 intersect N not inside b. By (b') of BCM's proof of Theorem 7.1 (read in the text: "lambda^b_i Tukey-below S_i intersect N") there is a family {s_i : i < lambda^b_1} in S_1 intersect N with no upper bound in S_1 intersect N. The union of the Y'_{s_i} is not null. So add(SN, N) <= lambda^b_1 = add(N) in the final model. Not checked by me: the construction of N in [CM22, Sec. 5], which BCM cite without proof for (a')-(c'); the link between E_b^h and B_b^h.
Side remark, not proved: in the GKMS construction (1906.06608, Section 3) the LCU_1-spectrum argument shows the final value lambda_7 of add(N) arises from theta_6 = add(N)^pre, which suggests cf(sup(theta_6 intersect N*)) = lambda_7. So the linear route probably works there, with theta = the P^pre value of add(N).

CLAIM 4(b): correctly marked unproved. Not checked by me either.

CLAIM 5: a status report, acceptable. Unproved sketch for (i): for an elementary embedding j : V -> M with M closed under countable sequences, j(P) is ccc, M and V have the same nice j(P)-names of reals, and "p forces x in the intersection of the [sigma_alpha]_infinity over alpha in Z, and x not in G" is absolute between M and V. If j"theta_1 is cofinal in j(theta_1), the linear witness of length theta_1 survives. I did not check the iterands of the Goldstern-Kellner-Shelah initial forcing, so this stays unproved.

CLAIM 6: sound. U*_K is a Q-invariant Borel set of measure < 1, hence null by the 0-1 law. A null G gives a null Q-invariant set G + Q, which misses some K; invariance gives G inside U*_K. So the family {U*_K} is cofinal and sel >= cof(N).

SUMMARY SECTION
- "(a) no set of size cof(N) is well-ordered by a Borel relation" is stated without proof. It is true. Proof: let R be Borel and well-order X, and suppose mu*(X) > 0 for an atomless finite Borel mu. Take an initial segment X' of least order type with mu*(X') > 0. X' has no largest element and every proper initial segment is mu-null. Let H be a Borel hull of X'; then mu(B intersect H) = mu*(B intersect X') for Borel B. For y in X', mu({x : xRy} intersect H) = 0; for x in X', mu({y : xRy} intersect H) = mu(H). Both hold on Borel sets containing X', hence for almost every point of H. Fubini gives (mu x mu)(R intersect H^2) = 0 and = mu(H)^2 > 0. Contradiction. Attribution (Reclaw, Plewik) not checked.
- "(c) the forcing must use iterands that are not theta-R^pt-good" is overstated. 5.18 constrains only finite support iterations of its shape. Countable support, creature, template and shattered constructions are outside it. Also "strong-measure-zero sets" there should be "universally null sets".
